evidence.title: Feasibility of autonomous medication delivery robots considering elevator utilization in high-traffic hospital environments
evidence.publisher: Digital Health / SAGE; full text in PMC
evidence.publication_date_basis: EuropePMC primary JATS epub date 31 March 2026; DOI search metadata February 1 conflicts and is not selected
evidence.geography: Korea University Guro Hospital, Seoul, Republic of Korea
evidence.verification: Full primary text retrieved through Exa and public EuropePMC JATS API; methods/results/limitations inspected.
evidence.claim: One robot on a routine pharmacy-to-emergency-department route; 135 requests, 13 urgent exclusions, 122 eligible missions, 14 reported failures and 108 completed missions. Trained operator accompanied robot; pharmacists/support staff/nurses handled load/retrieval. Reported 87.03 percent success conflicts with counts.
limitations: Single robot/site, short prospective feasibility window, selected nonurgent missions; no matched timed human courier control.
Four-week survey phase wording differs from June 18–29 mission window; relation not reconciled.
Raw datasets available from corresponding author upon request; no public mission dataset retrieved and no outreach authorized.
No complete escort/support duration, operating-hour exposure, intervention-event count or cost denominator.
Site-specific 59.01 percent elevator-usage threshold was fitted within this dataset; no prospective randomized dispatch-policy trial.

evidence.title: The effect of autonomous mobile robots on improving endoscope reprocessing efficiency: a prospective comparative trial (with video)
evidence.authors: Yuqing Shi, Jianrong Bai, Meiling Zhou et al.
evidence.publication_date_basis: PubMed primary HTML and EFetch XML directly verify electronic publication on October 10, 2025; journal issue is May 2026. An earlier indexed publisher-history extract gave October 9, but that history was not reproduced in the current fetch and is retained only as a metadata discrepancy.
evidence.geography: Qilu Hospital of Shandong University, Jinan, China
evidence.verification: Primary publisher and PubMed abstracts inspected. PubMed HTML and EFetch XML directly verify the electronic date and Shinva affiliations. The fulltext-named publisher URL yielded abstract/references, not detailed methods; direct publisher retrieval returned HTTP 403. Do not imply full-method verification.
evidence.locator: Abstract Methods/Results; publisher Publication History and affiliations
evidence.claim: One manual transport day randomly selected each five-day week, four AMR days; 5393 manual and 21048 AMR-assisted deliveries included; 8 AMRs; lower reported distribution/retrieval mean times and 0.15 percent AMR delivery failure rate. Authors report 2.18 FTE workload reduction and 12.8 percent ROI.
limitations: Randomization is by day, not individual delivery; day clustering, route/order mix and adjusted analysis unavailable in accessible abstract.
Definition of included delivery versus accepted completion, failed-case timing treatment and phase-specific sample sizes are not exposed.
Loading/unloading, exception handling, cleaning/reprocessing, staff monitoring and maintenance minutes are not separately exposed.
FTE and ROI calculation methods/cost boundary inaccessible; reported figures are not accepted calibration.
Transport elapsed-time contrasts do not establish paid labor removal, nursing substitution or humanoid economics.
evidence.author_context: PubMed HTML/XML lists Jun Cheng and Xiaoming Zhu at Shinva Medical Instrument Co, Ltd, Zibo, Shandong, China. The abstract disclosure states no conflicts related to this study. Affiliation does not establish a conflict or an independent financial audit.
evidence.metadata_locator: PubMed: citation_author_institution/expanded affiliations and Epub date; EFetch XML: ArticleDate[@DateType="Electronic"] and AuthorList/Author/AffiliationInfo for Jun Cheng and Xiaoming Zhu.

evidence.title: Integrating Collaborative Robots into a Complex Hospital Setting
evidence.verification: Primary full text inspected during this session's independent market review; retained here only for continuity of the denominator gap.
evidence.claim: 23 observation sessions, 33 observer-hours, 89 end-to-end deliveries; 107 headline interventions versus categories totaling 111.
limitations: Observer-hours are not automatically robot operating-hours or paid support-hours.
No intervention-duration series or representative current-platform staffing denominator.
No follow-up source retrieved here resolves 107 versus 111; do not replace either number or combine with later cumulative deliveries.

evidence.publication_date_basis: Issuu publisher record date; ChristianaCare page embeds this report. Not a verified report revision/effective date.
evidence.observation_period: Report describes multi-year ChristianaCare initiative; detailed contents not retrieved
evidence.verification: Operator landing page and embedded report metadata retrieved. Issuu text extraction returned title/description only; direct report/embed requests 403.
evidence.locator: Operator landing-page introduction and Issuu publication metadata

limitations: Report contents not source-verified in this wave.

configured_system.robot: DOGU IROI, one Level 3+ medication-delivery robot as classified by authors
configured_system.integration: Web request, secure drawer, TK50M staff-only shared elevator with communication module; 1 Hz elevator/robot logs
configured_system.workflow: Support staff dispatch; pharmacist loads/starts; robot travels pharmacy B2F to emergency department 1F; support staff or nurse retrieves medication.
configured_system.alternative: Existing support-staff manual courier route, not measured in a matched time/cost comparison

cases.accepted_output_definition: The paper defines success as the robot "completing the entire route and handing over the medication without any human intervention" (Section 2.4).
cases.failure_definition: Stationary for more than 1 minute at any point OR manual assistance due to passenger/cargo obstruction. Failed missions are not equivalent to intervention-event count.

exposure.missingness_reason: Calendar window and sampled requests provided; no aggregate matched robot/observer/paid-support duration.

metrics.denominator: described by authors as all trials; inconsistent with other counts
missions with EOR < 59.01 percent; subgroup size not extracted
one-hour window assigned by mission start hour

metrics.period: survey after described four-week phase; relationship to mission dates unresolved

human_support.safety_accompaniment: A trained operator accompanied the robot for medication-handling safety and annotations. This presence coexists with the paper's literal "without any human intervention" success definition; distinguishing presence from corrective assistance is our contextual interpretation.
human_support.normal_handling: Request/dispatch, pharmacy loading/start, destination retrieval/verification and subsequent handoff remain human tasks.
human_support.failure_recovery: Failure modes recorded; response duration, staffing identity, recovery attempts and final medication delivery not quantified.
human_support.support_minutes_missingness_reason: Failed-mission definition includes timeout without required manual assistance; no support-duration data or matched accepted-output denominator.

service_quality.urgent_delivery: 13 urgent requests excluded; service is nonurgent.
service_quality.success_rate_missingness_reason: Reported 87.03 percent conflicts with 108 completed/122 eligible; preserve conflict until source resolves.
service_quality.timing_boundary: Elevator delay analysis uses 108 completed trials, excluding failed missions. Table 1 wait/travel definitions differ slightly from Section 3.4 prose; do not reconstruct full service cycle from plot correlations.
service_quality.burden: No significant overall NASA-TLX differences across occupational groups; support staff median SUS about 77.5, but nurses/pharmacists acquire microtasks. Survey is not measured labor minutes.
service_quality.threshold_policy_status: Avoiding congestion is a proposed dispatch strategy. Low-congestion subgroup success is not causal benefit of deploying such a policy; filtering non-elevator failures cannot establish all-cause 100 percent reliability.

cases.permitted_use: Measure failure modes, mission selection and required staffing dimensions; test congestion-aware dispatch locally. No wage, staffing or universal reliability coefficient.
cases.definition_interpretation: Our contextual interpretation distinguishes corrective assistance from routine loading, retrieval and safety accompaniment, because Sections 2.3–2.4 disclose those human roles. The paper does not formally delimit the intervention term; preserve the tension between its literal definition and the staffed workflow.

configured_system.robot: Eight AMRs in an endoscope distribution/retrieval system; model/version not verified from accessible abstract.
configured_system.integration: Outpatient endoscopy rooms and reprocessing transport; detailed integration boundary not retrieved.
configured_system.workflow: Distribution and retrieval of endoscopes, not clinical endoscopy itself or autonomous reprocessing.
configured_system.alternative: Manual transport on one randomly selected day in each five-day week; AMR transport on remaining four days.

cases.accepted_output_definition_missingness_r: Abstract says included deliveries and gives failure rate, but does not expose attempt/completion counting or required quality acceptance rules.

exposure.missingness_reason: Delivery totals and calendar design do not expose operating hours or staff support time; 21048 cannot be multiplied by phase means to recover labor.

service_quality.end_to_end_clinical_quality: Adverse-event outcome listed, but detailed event definitions/results not exposed; no sterility/patient-outcome equivalence assumed.

cases.permitted_use: Retain phase-time benchmark as comparative source evidence; prioritize obtaining FTE/support calculation methods. Do not use reported FTE/ROI as common engine assumptions.

calculations.interpretation: 90.37 percent of logged requests enter the nonurgent study; this is selection coverage for this sample, not all hospital demand eligibility.
calculations.denominator: 135 logged delivery requests, including the 13 urgent requests excluded from the eligible-mission analysis.
calculations.population: Requests logged for one DOGU IROI pharmacy-to-emergency-department route at Korea University Guro Hospital; this is study-selection coverage.

calculations.interpretation: 57.14 percent of classified failures were elevator blockages. Not intervention rate, staffing ratio or fraction of all service time.
calculations.denominator: 14 classified failed missions; the numerator is the eight elevator-blockage failures.
calculations.population: Failure-type composition among the reported failed nonurgent missions on the Guro study route; not all requests, intervention events or service time.

calculations.interpretation: 88.52 percent from stated counts differs from reported 87.03 percent by 1.49459 percentage points. Preserve both; no invented reconciliation or preferred rate.
calculations.denominator: 122 eligible nonurgent missions; the numerator is the 108 completed trials reported in the timing analysis.
calculations.population: Guro study mission cohort, evaluated only as a count-consistency audit; conflict with the published overall success percentage remains unresolved.

calculations.unit: seconds difference in reported distribution means
calculations.interpretation: Reported AMR distribution mean is 56.41 seconds or 33.48 percent lower. This is a contrast of phase means, not measured person-time savings or an accepted full-service rate.
calculations.denominator: Published distribution-phase group means; the relative contrast divides by the manual mean of 168.48 seconds. Phase-specific sample counts are not exposed.
calculations.population: Qilu outpatient endoscope distribution: manual-day and AMR-assisted-day group means within the comparative study, not pooled delivery counts or measured person-time.

calculations.unit: seconds difference in reported retrieval means
calculations.interpretation: Reported AMR retrieval mean is 21.36 seconds or 23.39 percent lower. Do not sum with distribution to infer person-time without matched pairing and timing methods.
calculations.denominator: Published retrieval-phase group means; the relative contrast divides by the manual mean of 91.32 seconds. Phase-specific sample counts are not exposed.
calculations.population: Qilu outpatient endoscope retrieval: manual-day and AMR-assisted-day group means within the comparative study, not pooled delivery counts or measured person-time.

conflicts.model_action: Keep observation dates and survey phase separately labeled.

conflicts.resolution_missingness_reason: Existing conflict preserved; operator blueprint text not retrieved and no new resolving source found.
conflicts.model_action: Do not calculate a current intervention/staffing rate or combine with 48, 600 later cumulative deliveries.

missing_denominator_contract.accepted_output: Unique request ID, payload/service standard, urgency, destination receipt, quality/timeliness acceptance, manual fallback outcome.
missing_denominator_contract.exposure: Robot active/idle/down hours for the same missions, staff observation windows and failed/cancelled request inclusion.
missing_denominator_contract.normal_support: Timed preparation/loading/unloading/verification, dispatch/monitoring, cleaning/charging and coordination by role.
missing_denominator_contract.exception_support: Time-to-detect/respond/recover; number of people and assistance episodes; remote/on-site distinction; eventual accepted service.
missing_denominator_contract.comparator: Matched route, urgency, payload mix, time of day and service quality for human/digital/specialized alternatives.
missing_denominator_contract.economic_bridge: Avoidable paid labor versus redeployment; costs and overhead; no automatic multiplication of elapsed phase time by delivery count.
missing_denominator_contract.prospective_policy_test: Congestion-aware dispatch must report deferred/urgent/manual deliveries and delay distribution, not only success of selected low-traffic runs.

model_constraints: Existing common-model calibration unchanged; support_minutes_per_accepted_delivery remains unknown in both cases.
Failure or no-correction success is distinct from human presence and normal handling labor.
Calendar duration, sampled missions and cumulative deliveries are not interchangeable exposure denominators.
Selection of nonurgent or low-congestion jobs changes service coverage and may shift urgent/fallback work to humans.
Comparative phase-time improvement and workloadFTE are distinct from payroll removal, financing return and humanoid advantage.
Current US hospital cell may use these cases only as mechanism/comparator evidence until target-side validation.
